hypothesis: The parent (c007) enables timing-driven net weighting but relies on the default `momentum_decay_factor` for the Adam-style criticality momentum; lowering it makes the criticality signal track the *current* placement more responsively each iteration, so many moderately-critical nets keep meaningful weight instead of being dominated by a few early-identified critical nets — spreading buffer-friendly weight across more violating paths and reducing TNS.
analysis: The hypothesis held: all three cases improved, with dWNS +10.8–15.6% and dTNS +4.9–25.9%, robust score +0.098 and min_case +0.077. The mechanism fits—lower momentum decay lets criticality track current placement, spreading weight to moderately-critical nets rather than a few early nets, reducing TNS (largest gain on ariane133, +25.9%). Overflow ~90–127 suggests routing pressure worth watching. Next step: sweep `momentum_decay_factor` across a small grid (e.g., 0.5×, 0.25× default) on these cases to confirm monotonic benefit and check overflow/routability doesn't degrade.
